sourcingNote: Token/complexity defaults are illustrative starting points based on common patterns for each use-case type, not measured benchmarks. All fields are user-editable in the app — treat these as reasonable defaults, not facts about any specific deployment.

useCases.label: Knowledge / HR / IT assistant
useCases.description: Answers employee questions against a defined, relatively narrow set of internal policy/process content.
useCases.suggestedArchitecture: Simple prompt + light context (may not need full RAG if source content is small)

useCases.label: Customer service chatbot
useCases.description: Conversational, history-aware support interactions, often with escalation paths to a human.

useCases.label: RAG / enterprise search
useCases.description: Retrieval-augmented generation over a larger, less curated document corpus.
useCases.suggestedArchitecture: Retrieval + generation (vector search or hybrid search feeding the prompt)

useCases.label: Coding assistant
useCases.description: Code generation, review, or debugging assistance. Often licensed per-seat rather than raw API in practice — flagged here as a caveat, not modeled as a licensing cost.
useCases.suggestedArchitecture: Often a per-seat tool license rather than raw token billing

useCases.label: Single agent (tool-using)
useCases.description: One agent making multiple tool calls in a chain to complete a task.

useCases.label: Multi-agent workflow
useCases.description: Multiple specialised agents collaborating on a task, each with its own call chain.
useCases.suggestedArchitecture: Multiple coordinated agents, often with an orchestrator
useCases.costMultiplierNote: Apply a 1.5x-3x multiplier over a single-agent base estimate for retries/loops, per common agentic-workload patterns.

useCases.label: Classification / extraction
useCases.description: High-volume, low-complexity structured tasks — labeling, tagging, field extraction.
useCases.suggestedArchitecture: Small/cheap model, high volume, often batched

useCases.label: Custom / other
useCases.description: Use case doesn't fit the categories above, or the underlying task isn't token-based LLM economics at all (e.g. traditional ML/forecasting) — flag this rather than force-fitting it.
